<br>

This r markdown (.rmd) file takes the updated meta data files (which have been previously filtered) and replaces the old meta data file in a phyloseq object

The phyloseq object contains meta data (demographic & clinical data for participants), otu data, taxanomic data, and a phylogenetic tree

Code on how to pull each of these data from the phyloseq object are provided below 

Notes about the data:

Meta data

* 150 participants with 495 stool samples across BL, 3m, 6m, and 12m timepoints 
* Long table with repeating rows for participants at various timepoints (e.g. unique SampleIDs [AAL-144.12m], but repeating RID [144] & subject_id [AAL-144])
* Variables:
  - IDs: SampleID, RID, subject_id 
  - Intervention (character) and imf (binary: 0/1)
  - Covariates: 
      - age
      - sex (0/1) and sex_cat
      - race and race_cat with 3 categories (Black, White, Other with White as referent)
      - ethnicity (0/1)
  - Timepoint (BL, 3m, 6m, 12m)
  - Time (0, 3, 6, 12)
  - Outcomes (raw, absolute change, and % change): 
      - Primary: weight and wc
      - Secondary: BMI, MetS, HOMA-IR, HbA1c, WBTOT, RMR, adherence, calories
      - Possibly: 
          - appetite hormone: Ghrelin, Peptide YY, Leptin, Adiponectin
          - CRP, BP, Cholesterol (Total, HDL, LDL, Triglycerides)
          - Adiponectin/Leptin ratio
  - Alpha diversity measures: shannon_entropy, observed_features, pielou_evenness, faith_pd

### Data Preparation  
```{r}
# load in the new meta data file using the fread() function from the data.table package

meta_sub <- fread(file='C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/DRIFT_long_metadata_microbiome_092026.csv')
# can view data by clicking on the newly loaded in data table in the environment to the right or use: 
view(meta_sub)
# this file is a long format data table with repeating rows for participants 
dim(meta_sub)
#[1] 495  40
# 495 rows/samples with 40 columns/variables 
length(unique(meta_sub$subject_id.x))
#[1] 150
# 150 unique participants

meta_sub_wide <- fread(file='C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/DRIFT_wide_metadata_microbiome_092026.csv')
# this file is a wide format data table with only 1 row per participant 

# load in phyloseq object using load(
load("C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/PhyloseqObj_Updated_N150_092026.RData")
#load(file='/Users/ashleyward/Desktop/DRIFT2_microbiome/Updated/DRIFT2.Phylo.COUNT.R21116.0923.RData')
#load(file='/Users/ashleyward/Desktop/DRIFT2_microbiome/Updated/DRIFT2.Phylo.RA.0923.RData')
#load(file='/Users/ashleyward/Desktop/DRIFT2_microbiome/Updated/DRIFT2.Phylo.CLR.0923.RData')

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
#refactor variables
meta_sub$Timepoint <- factor(meta_sub$Timepoint, lev=c('BL', '3m', '6m', '12m'))
meta_sub$Intervention<- factor(meta_sub$Intervention, lev=c('IMF', 'DCR'))
meta_sub$imf<- factor(meta_sub$imf, lev=c('1','0'))
# 1 (IMF) is referent 

meta_sub$race_cat_3<- factor(meta_sub$race_cat_3, lev=c('White','Black/African American', 'Other'))

meta_sub$ethnicity_cat<- factor(meta_sub$ethnicity_cat, lev=c('Not Hispanic/Latino','Hispanic/Latino'))

```


### Replace meta data in phyloseq object
```{r}

#starting with CLR transformed data
#pull the OTU, taxomony, and phylogentic trees from the phyloseq object and give them unique names
otu <- otu_table(drift.phy.clr) #the otu table is organized with the OTUs as rownames and SampleIDs as columns
otu_as_df <- as.data.frame(otu)
dim(otu)
rownames(otu)
colnames(otu)
tax <- tax_table(drift.phy.clr) #the taxonomy is organized with the OTUs as rownames and Taxonomic Ranks as columns
tree <- phy_tree(drift.phy.clr) #the tree is a list where the tip.labels are the OTUs

#ensure meta data is properly formatted
meta_data <- as.data.frame(meta_sub)
rownames(meta_data) <- meta_data$SampleID
meta_sd <- sample_data(meta_data)

# Check the data types
class(otu)
class(tax)
class(meta_sd)
class(tree)

#remake the phyloseq object with these components 
drift.phy.clr <- phyloseq(otu, tax, meta_sd, tree)


drift.phy.clr

#the new phyloseq object contains 495 samples 
nsamples(drift.phy.clr)

#repeat for the other phyloseq objects

#raw read counts
otu <- otu_table(drift.phy.count)
tax <- tax_table(drift.phy.count)
tree <- phy_tree(drift.phy.count)

drift.phy.count <- phyloseq(otu, tax, meta_sd, tree)

drift.phy.count
nsamples(drift.phy.count)

#rarefied count data
otu <- otu_table(drift.phy.count.r21116)
tax <- tax_table(drift.phy.count.r21116)
tree <- phy_tree(drift.phy.count.r21116)

drift.phy.count.r21116 <- phyloseq(otu, tax, meta_sd, tree)

drift.phy.count.r21116
nsamples(drift.phy.count.r21116)

#relative abundance
otu <- otu_table(drift.phy.ra)
tax <- tax_table(drift.phy.ra)
tree <- phy_tree(drift.phy.ra)

drift.phy.ra <- phyloseq(otu, tax, meta_sd, tree)

drift.phy.ra
nsamples(drift.phy.ra)
```

### Save updated phyloseq objects
```{r}
save(drift.phy.clr, drift.phy.count, drift.phy.count.r21116, drift.phy.ra, 
     file='C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/PhyloseqObj_Updated_N150_092026.RData')
```
